caption:
Flood season and pipeline theft season overlap in the Niger Delta. That is not coincidence.

When creeks and swamp forest flood, foot and boat patrol access drops. Illegal tapping points are harder to reach and easier to work unseen. The same standing water that raises flood risk also degrades the ground response to theft.

Upstream, the mechanics are separate but structurally similar: release timing on transboundary dams sits with another country's authority, and the flood that reaches Nigerian floodplains is the result of a decision made outside Nigerian jurisdiction. Two different risk domains, same lesson — the terrain and the authority that shapes it are rarely in the same place as the consequence.

Planning that treats flood risk and pipeline security as unrelated seasonal problems is planning against last year's map.

card.headline: Flood season hides the tap
card.sub: Rising water cuts patrol access to Delta creeks in the same window pipeline theft peaks. Two risks, one terrain problem.

rationale: Introduces a fresh, publicly-grounded synthesis (flood terrain degrading anti-theft patrol access) distinct from prior dam- and theft-economics posts, keeping the CONTEXT pillar's analytic register without repeating phrasing or claiming a detection.
